question:
The bar graph given below shows the selling price of 6 given articles.

Selling price = Cost price times [1 + (Profit%/100)]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f69cc75066f018d29a93ff75862869c50b8c81fdcfe3f232d11632009614556e.png] 

Profit earned on article F is 30 percent. What is the cost price of article F?
solution:
**Given:**

 
 

 Article
 Selling Price
 
 

 A
 660
 
 

 B
 960
 
 

 C
 770
 
 

 D
 1125
 
 

 E
 990
 
 

 F
 600
 
 

Profit percentage earned on article F = 30%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price = Cost Price × [1 + (Profit% ÷ 100)]

Cost Price = Selling Price ÷ [1 + (Profit% ÷ 100)]

**Calculation:**

According to the question and the data from the graph,

⇒ Selling price of article F = 600

⇒ Profit percentage on article F = 30%

⇒ Cost price of article F = 600 ÷ [1 + (30 ÷ 100)]

⇒ Cost price of article F = 600 ÷ [1 + 0.3]

⇒ Cost price of article F = 600 ÷ 1.3

⇒ Cost price of article F = 6000 ÷ 13

⇒ Cost price of article F ≈ 461.5384...

⇒ Cost price of article F ≈ 461.54

**∴ The correct answer is 461.54.**
